objective: Classify the 100 proposed Forest-First improvements against live Federation capability so new work extends or composes existing primitives instead of creating duplicate systems.
frontier_benchmark_lessons: Prefer a small number of composable primitives over additional named agent brains.
Treat tracing, handoffs, guardrails, durable state and human approvals as explicit contracts.
Durable workflows require replay-safe/idempotent interrupt boundaries and exact state restoration.
Empirical evals should be built from real traces and measured outcomes rather than source sophistication.
Forest-First already exceeds generic agent frameworks in explicit proof/authority/rollback boundaries; its main gaps are universal typed contracts, simplicity and measured fitness.
